title: Minimum Index Sum of Common Elements
summary: Given two equal-length integer arrays, find the minimum sum of indices for matching elements across the arrays; return -1 if no matches exist.
statement: Given two equal-length integer arrays, find the minimum sum of indices for matching elements across the arrays; return -1 if no matches exist.
constraints: Equal-length arrays contain up to 100,000 signed integers.
A good pair holds equal values across the arrays.
Return the minimum i+j, or negative one if none exists.
hints: For a fixed value, only its earliest position in the second array can minimize a sum.
Build an earliest-index map, then scan the first array and minimize i+map[value].
Preserve the first occurrence in nums2 and return negative one when no mapped value appears.
Replacing either index by a later occurrence cannot improve the sum, so the map loses no optimum.
editorial: Replacing either index by a later occurrence cannot improve the sum, so the map loses no optimum.

tests.explanation: Value three at indices zero and one gives the minimum sum one.
Values one and two both achieve index sum two.
